Question

What is the research process in the West region?

Research:

One of your duties as a Retrieval Specialist include researching however if you have made your efforts and cannot locate anything, the order can be sent to Samantha Richards.

Ex: The client requested records from a facility that you cannot locate via Google.

Ex: If we are searching for a specific doctor and have followed up with several facilities but no one has any current follow up information

- Status with "Research Required"
- Email Samantha the WO. Samantha will perform her own research and send the order where it needs to go.

Question

What is the scheduling process in the West region for California only?

If records are ready to be picked up or copied, schedule accordingly. Make sure you ask all of the questions below completely as your driver does not have Wincopy to verify information. If an appointment is necessary, request at least a two-hour window as your driver may run into traffic or have trouble finding parking and ask for a back-up date/time in case the first option is not available. But before you schedule, you must first reach out to the Field Department Management Team to confirm if there will be a driver available.

VERIFY YOUR INFORMATION

· Are we picking up or copying? (THIS MAKES A BIG DIFFERENCE IN THE DRIVER'S TRIP)

- If copy, verify how many inches so that your driver has an idea on how long it will take

(Generally, 1 inch can take anywhere from 20-30 minutes)

· What are the days and hours our driver can go? (Ex: M-F 8-12/1-5; Tues & Thurs 8-12; Fridays Only 8-5) -Is a specific appointment necessary, if so follow the above instructions

· If the order is requesting billing records, Is billing included?

-If yes, make sure to list it (Ex: medical and billing records)

INFORMATION 45 CFR 164.508 (c)(1)(i) A description of the information to be disclosed that identifies the information in a specific and meaningful fashion.

DISCLOSING ENTITY 45 CFR 164.508 (c)(1)(ii) The name or other specific identification of the person(s), or class of persons, authorized to make the disclosure.

RECIPIENT 45 CFR 164.508 (c)(1)(iii) The name or other specific identification of the person(s), or class of persons, to whom the covered entity may make the requested disclosure.

PURPOSE 45 CFR 164.508 (c)(1)(iv) A description of each purpose of the requested use or disclosure. The statement "at the request of the individual" is a sufficient description of the purpose when an individual initiates the authorization an does not, or elects not to, provide a statement of the purpose.

EXPIRATION DATE 45 CFR 164.508 (c)(1)(v) An expiration date or an expiration event that relates to the use or disclosure.

SIGNATURE 45 CFR 164.508 (c)(1)(vi) Signature of the individual and date. A copy of a signature is sufficient if the document states "a copy shall be considered as original".

text:

Topic: RISK REGION PROCEDURES > DEPOSITION SUBPOENA

A Deposition Subpoena is a request for records. By law, the subpoena provides a maximum of 15 days from the date of service for the facility to comply. Records obtained from any facility with this type of request will always require that an affidavit be accompanied indicating whether they have records or not. Federal, Out-of-State, requests for "sensitive" records, and Native American locations are not bound by California subpoenas as the request either lacks sufficient authority or there is no jurisdiction.

DISCOVERY- Pre-trial method for obtaining facts and information about the case from the other party or witnesses. Discovery is the process used by attorneys to prepare for trial (up to 30 days before trial) or arbitration (up to 15 days before arbitration). Discovery includes depositions, interrogations, subpoenas, production of documents/things, obtaining medical and business records, etc.

DISCOVERY CUT OFF- The time in which discovery must stop.

D.O.B. - Date of birth of the claimant/patient.

D.O.S. - Date of service. The date in which services were rendered for the claimant/patient.

DUE DATE- The date that the records are due in our client's office. (This is usually the same as the depo date)

DUE DILIGENCE- Everything we did to get records. (Our statuses in Wincopy notates all of our due diligence)

EXECUTORSHIP PAPERS- Documents that indicate the person(s) authorized to obtain information on a deceased claimant.

FACILITY- The hospital, clinic, or healthcare facility where the patient's records are located and can be obtained.

FEES- A location can charge us a fee to obtain records, films, photos, etc.

MEDICAL LIEN: The right of a hospital, doctor or health care provider to assert an interest in personal injury recoveries to the extent of the cost of the treatment or service provided. MOTION TO COMPEL- A document from the court requiring the location/facility to release records.

MOTION TO QUASH- A legal document filed with the court demanding all work be stopped immediately on every location listed on the motion. There will be a hearing date listed on the motion at which time all parties will go before the judge and present their case as to why or why not the records should or should not be made available to copy.

NEXT OF KIN- The person in a family to be successor after a family member has been Diseased. (The wife is deceased; her husband would be the successor.)

NON-CONSUMER- Records of property or things that are not owned by an individual or group.

OBJECTION- When one does not agree that records should be released either because the request is too broad or the location's records are not pertinent to the case.

ORDER TO SHOW CAUSE- A document from the court requiring the C/R to appear before the judge and give good cause as to why they did not comply with the subpoena or other types of court requests.

PATIENT- An individual awaiting or under medical care and treatment.

PERSONAL APPEARANCE SUBPOENA- A subpoena that requires a person to either appear at court with or without records, or in lieu of an appearance, mail the records directly to the court.

PITCHESS MOTION- In order to obtain personnel records of any peace officer in California, a "Pitches" motion is require to be filed with the court and granted by a judge in order to obtain the records.

PLAINTIFF- The individual or business that has made the claim/law suit.

SUBPOENA DUCES TECUM (SDT) - a writ commanding a person to produce in court certain designated documents or evidence (Duces Tecum – Latin for Records)

SUBPOENAING PARTY- The party or person who is causing the subpoena to be issued.

SUBSTITUTION OF ATTORNEY- When one attorney or their client determines a new attorney may be able to represent the client better.

SUMMONS- A document notifying a party or parties they are being sued and the time frame in which they must respond to the court with their version with regards to the action being brought against them.

TRIAL- The examination before a judicial tribunal of the facts put in issue in a cause, often including issues of the law as well as those of fact.

WET SIGNATURE- The original blue ink signature on the Subpoena being provided after requested by a custodian of records (AKA: Original Signature from Attorney)

WITNESS- A person who has information about the subject matter of a lawsuit, but who is not a party (plaintiff or defendant) involved in the lawsuit.

WORKERS' COMPENSATION- Legally mandated provisions for awards to an employee or their dependents in case of employment related accidents or diseases.

text:
Document: Southeast
Topic: SOUTHEAST REGION PROCEDURES > 8. HIPAA Compliance Checklist for Authorizations > 8.1 Required Authorization Elements

Table:
Element | CFR Reference | Requirement
Information to Be Disclosed | 45 CFR 164.508(c)(1)(i) | The authorization must clearly and specifically describe the information to be used or disclosed
Disclosing Entity | 45 CFR 164.508(c)(1)(ii) | The authorization must identify the person or organization permitted to disclose the information
Recipient | 45 CFR 164.508(c)(1)(iii) | The authorization must identify the person or organization permitted to receive the information
Purpose | 45 CFR 164.508(c)(1)(iv) | The authorization must describe the purpose of the requested use or disclosure
Expiration Date or Event | 45 CFR 164.508(c)(1)(v) | The authorization must include an expiration date or an event related to the purpose of the disclosure
Signature and Date | 45 CFR 164.508(c)(1)(vi) | The authorization must be signed and dated by the individual or authorized representative
Right to Revoke | 45 CFR 164.508(c)(2)(i) | The authorization must explain the individual’s right to revoke and how revocation may be completed
No Conditions | 45 CFR 164.508(c)(2)(ii) | Treatment, payment, enrollment, or benefit eligibility generally cannot be conditioned on signing the authorization
Potential for Redisclosure | 45 CFR 164.508(c)(2)(iii) | The authorization must explain that disclosed information may be subject to redisclosure
Plain Language | 45 CFR 164.508(c)(3) | The authorization must be written in language that is clear and understandable
Copy to the Individual | 45 CFR 164.508(c)(4) | The individual must receive a copy of the signed authorization when required

Topic: SOUTHEAST REGION PROCEDURES > 9. Types of Requests > 9.1 Signed Authorization

Definition

A Signed Authorization is a request signed by the patient or authorized representative that permits the release of records.

Requirements

The authorization must identify the patient.
It must clearly describe the records requested.
It must comply with applicable state and federal privacy requirements.
It must include the required signature and date.
It must not be expired.

Important Note

Review the authorization using the HIPAA Compliance Checklist before submitting it to the facility.

Topic: SOUTHEAST REGION PROCEDURES > 9. Types of Requests > 9.2 Deposition Subpoena

Definition

A Deposition Subpoena is a legal request requiring a facility or custodian to produce records.

General Requirements

The facility generally has a limited period from the date of service to comply.
The request may require an affidavit confirming whether responsive records exist.
The applicable response period and affidavit requirements may depend on jurisdiction and request type.

Possible Exceptions

Additional documentation or procedures may be required for:

Federal requests
Out-of-state requests
Sensitive records
Native American facilities
Facilities not subject to the issuing jurisdiction
Requests requiring patient authorization

An affidavit may identify:

The records released
The person or organization receiving the records
The facility releasing the records
Whether no records exist
Whether the records provided are complete

Affidavits provide documentation supporting the facility’s response and may confirm that all available records have been supplied.

Nevada Requirement

For Nevada requests, confirm whether the affidavit must be notarized before accepting it.

Topic: SOUTHEAST REGION PROCEDURES > 11. HIPAA Law

Purpose

HIPAA establishes federal privacy and security standards for protecting medical records and other protected health information.

HIPAA Privacy Rule

The HIPAA Privacy Rule:

Requires safeguards for protected health information
Limits certain uses and disclosures without valid authorization
Establishes conditions for permissible disclosures
Gives individuals rights concerning their health information
Requires covered entities to follow applicable privacy procedures

Regulatory Location

The HIPAA Privacy Rule is primarily located in:

45 CFR Part 160
45 CFR Part 164, Subparts A and E

Important Operational Rule

Do not disclose protected health information unless the request, authorization, subpoena, or other legal documentation satisfies the applicable requirements.

Identify available evidence

Gather sworn testimony
Understand the facts that may be presented at trial
Prepare their legal arguments

Depositions
Interrogatories
Requests for admissions

Topic: WEST REGION > 1. VOICEMAIL

Voicemail is an important tool we use here in Document Retrieval as we depend on it to receive any messages we have missed while we are on the phone or away from our desk.

- You must always remember to check your voicemail.
- Voicemails should be checked multiple times throughout the day.
- All calls must be returned.

Voicemail Greeting Example

"Hello and thank you for calling ABI Document Support Services. This is the desk of [Your first & last name]. I am either on another call or away from my desk. If your call is urgent please email me at [your email, spell out if needed]. Slowly and clearly state your name, call back number, the ABI reference number along with a brief message and I will return your call as soon as I can. Thank you and have a great day!"

Topic: WEST REGION > 2. SIGNATURE FOR EMAIL

Purpose

To change or create your email signature in Microsoft Outlook.

Procedure

1. Open Outlook.
2. Click File (top left).
3. Click Options (bottom left).
4. Click Mail (top left).
5. Scroll down to Compose Messages, scroll down to Create or modify signatures for messages; Select Signatures.
6. There are two options from here: NEW (Go to Step 7) or EDIT EXISTING (Go to Step 18).
7. If signature is NEW, select NEW.
8. Name your email signature.
9. Copy the email signature above and paste into the edit signature window.
10. Edit to include your information.
11. At the upper right corner of the signature box, choose your new email signature for both new emails and replies.
12. Go back to the Compose Messages Section and select Stationary (below signature option).
13. Click font (New mail messages) select Segoe UI size 12 in black.
14. Click OK.
15. Click font (replying or forwarding messages) select Segoe UI size 12 in black.
16. Click OK.
17. Click OK.
18. EDIT EXISTING. If signature just needs to be edited, select signature to be edited and make edits in signature box.
19. Choose your new email signature for both your new emails and replies (upper right corner). Hit OK.
20. Next click go back to Compose Messages and select stationery (below signature).
21. Click font (New mail messages) select Segoe UI size 12 in black.
22. Click OK.
23. Click font (replying or forwarding messages) select Segoe UI size 12 in black.
24. Click OK.
25. Click OK.
26. Open a new email to confirm your signature has been updated.

The Health Insurance Portability & Accountability Act (HIPAA) establishes standards to protect an individual's medical records and other personal health information. HIPAA has rules and requires safeguards that set limits and conditions on the uses and disclosures that could be made of such information without patient authorization. This gives the individual rights over their own health information. This Privacy Rule is located at 45 CFR part 160 ad subparts A and E Part 164.

Topic: WEST REGION > 5. AUDIT CRITERIA AND METRICS

Purpose

Audits will be ran to ensure that your statuses meet the needed criteria and that the correct procedures are being followed. Use these audits as a resource for learning from your mistakes.

Scoring

- You will be scored on 6 orders chosen at random within the past 48 hours.
- Your score will consist of a "Pass" or "Fail" from 8 requirements.
- Each "Pass" is 13% of your total score per order and each passing order is 17% from the overall audit score.
- A passing score is 96% or higher, meaning 3 errors or more will put you at a fail.
- You will have until your next audit to bring your score up, if necessary.

Performance Expectations

Once training is complete, you will be required to make 50 calls per day as well 24 completes.

Document: West
Topic: WEST REGION > 12. DOC PRO > 12.1 Workflows

All orders fall into systems called the Paper Workflow and Paperless Workflow. The Paper Workflow is used by other departments handling physical paper requests. As a Retrieval Specialist, everything will be done on the Paperless Workflow since all orders are handled electronically (paperless). In order for a request to move through the Paperless Workflow, it must first be made "Live". This is done by inputting the status "Sent-Records Retrieval-PAPERLESS". Within 2-3 minutes, another status will auto-generate confirming that order is Live and has made its way to our department, stating "Work Order Sent to Records Retrieval (solcomuser)". Once the order is on the Paperless Workflow, it is able to move smoothly within the different departments as needed. The order will "End" from the Paperless Workflow once the order is being closed or if the order is sent to the Field Department where it will be put on the Paper Workflow since Field only handles the physical paper copies. If an order happens to fall off of the Paperless Workflow for any reason, that order is now stuck and will not be able to move within the departments.

Topic: WEST REGION > DOCUMENTS

The DOCUMENTS window also known as, Solcom. This is where you can find all documents provided by the facility such as: Records received, invoices, rejection letters etc. Once you open DOCUMENTS, your order will populate on the left, double click the order to open the view options.

All documents will be listed and labeled on the right side, double click the document you wish to view, and a separate window will pop-out for you to review. The below labels are the most commonly used for our department.

- CHECK STUB - Invoices or the invoice target sheet with the cut check stub.
- FACILITY CUSTODIAN OF RECORD PACKET - The original serve packet for the facility.
- REQUESTED DOCUMENT FOR CUSTOMER - Records received.
- CLOSEOUT LETTER FOR WORKORDER - The status letter used to explain why the order is being closed out.
- CERTIFICATION OF NO RECORDS AVAILABLE - The signed Affidavit of No Records.
- DECLARATION OF PHOTOCOPIER - The signed Affidavit of Custodian of Records.
- REC RETREIVAL FACILITY CORRESPONDENCE - Correspondence, rejections and breakdowns.

This window will show all payments made for this location both by check and credit card. Listed is the check number, the date the check was cut, who the check is payable to and the amount paid.

- The facility information and a preview of the statuses (Statuses cannot be added or edited from this view)

Topic: WEST REGION > PRINTED CHECKS > 14.6 Statuses in Doc Pro

Topic: WEST REGION > PRINTING INSTRUCTIONS

- Should we be following up with a ROI/ Copy Service? If the prior statuses state that the order is handled by an ROI, we should be contacting the handling ROI for status and not the treating facility directly.

Topic: WEST REGION > 18. SCHEDULING

Key Information

If records are ready to be picked up or copied, schedule accordingly. Make sure you ask all of the questions below as your driver does not have DocPro to verify information:

- Are we picking up or copying? (THIS MAKES A BIG DIFFERENCE IN THE DRIVER'S TRIP)
- If copy, verify how many inches so that your driver has an idea on how long it will take (Generally, 1 inch can take anywhere from 20-30 minutes).
- What are the days and hours our driver can go? (Ex: M-F 8-12/1-5; Tues & Thurs 8-12; Fridays Only 8-5).
- If a specific appointment necessary, if so follow the below instructions (Ex: Monday, April 6th @ 10am).
- If the order is requesting billing records, Is billing included?
- If yes, make sure to list it (Ex: medical and billing records).
- If no, the facility needs to provide an explanation on the Affidavit as to why they do not have billing or where it can be obtained from.
- If the order is requesting Xrays, does their office perform any imaging in-house?
- If no, use the VPU/VTC status with "NO FILMS".
- If yes, verify if we are obtaining a breakdown and you will need to request an Xcopy.
- Verify the address that we are picking up/ copying from.
- Do we owe the facility any fees for their services? How much and who do we make the check payable to?

text:

Topic: WEST REGION > 20. ROI'S

Key Information

An ROI refers to a Third-Party Records Service who processes the request on behalf of the treating facility. Some locations may require us to serve the treating facility, then they will transfer the request to the ROI service themselves. Other locations may require us to upload the request to their portal in order to process. These ROI's will gather the records, provide us with status and invoice our office for their services.

There are a handful of ROI's that our Clerical Support Department handles as they alone have access and work in the ROI portals. (You can check your updated extension list to see who is handling which ROI's). The below ROI's are handled by our Support Department:

- Ciox/ Datavant
- Sharecare
- MRO
- Claimfox
- DMRS
- Chartrequest
- Chartswap
- Clearpath
- Medinform

When you are first informed that a location uses a third-party ROI and a Request ID/ Invoice Number is not yet available, update the order using "FACILITY-ORDER SENT TO ROI" (Status 2675). You can PEND for 10 days.

Once the Request ID/ Invoice Number is available with records/ correspondence pending, update the order using "ROI-IN PROGRESS" (Status 2806).

Topic: WEST REGION > 21. FOLLOW UP ORDERS

Key Information

Follow Up's are orders created from an original order by Client Relations or Clerical Support when something additional is needed, records are missing or to challenge a facility.

Follow ups from Clerical Support are orders that you request personally or will be requested from Quality Control (QC) due to documents missing when records are being processed.

Topic: WEST REGION > 21. FOLLOW UP ORDERS

- Bcopy: Specifically created for billing records.
- Xcopy: Specifically created for digital imaging ONLY, if they exist at the facility.
- Follow up for missing records: Created by Client Relations as the Client believes not all records were provided or if specific information is missing.
- Follow up for missing Affidavit of Custodian of Records: Created by Clerical Support to continue following up for the missing affidavit as records were previously provided without.
- Follow up to challenge CNR: Created by Client Relations if the Client provides some form of proof that records exist or if they provide additional information that may help the facility locate records.

Please note, when calling on a Follow Up order these SHOULD NOT be addressed the same as a new order. Meaning we should be specifying that records were previously received but something is missing or that a CNR was previously received but the Client has provided proof.

There are only 3 ways to close an order: with records, a signed Affidavit of No Records or with a Status Letter. The purpose of a Status Letter is to explain why the order needs to be closed or to clarify information and add support so that an order can be closed.

- Duplicates
- Offsites
- Verbal ANR Process
- Permanently Closed
- When the Custodian of Records is signed incorrectly
- When no Custodian of Records is provided

Topic: WEST REGION > 25. VERBAL ANR PROCESS

Key Information

The Verbal ANR Process is to assist with closing orders where we were previously informed that a CNR would be provided.

Procedure

When a facility informs you that a CNR will be sent to us, update the order using "AFFIDAVIT-NO RECORDS-FACILITY 1ST VERBAL". For the second and third attempts you will use the 2nd and 3rd verbal statuses.

If we still have not received the CNR by the fourth attempt, the order can be closed with the "AFFIDAVIT-NO RECORDS-FACILITY 4TH VERBAL" as a Status Letter. This way the order is no longer delayed, and we have done our diligence to obtain the CNR. In the event the CNR is received at a later time, a follow up will be created to process.

Topic: WEST REGION > 26. PROCESSING DUPLICATES

Key Information

You can only close an order out as a duplicate if everything being requested is exactly the same: the requesting client, customer code, dates requested and requested records. If any of this information is not the same, then we would need to treat the orders completely separate. The entity names and addresses may be different if the facility goes by several names or has different locations.

Procedure

- If the entity names are different, you will use "RECORDS-INCLUDED W/ ANOTHER-CLOSE" (Status 2648).
- If the entity names are the same, you will use "EXACT SAME ORDER-CLOSE" (Status 3379).

PLEASE REFER TO STEPS 1 - 5 IN "PROCESSING STATUS LETTER CLOSE OUTS".

- The Trigger will be "SENT-DUPLICATE REVIEW". The Team Lead will review the status letter and send it over to Production. If it needs to be returned for any corrections, the Lead will email you and/or send the order back to you in Solcom/ Documents.

Topic: WEST REGION > 28. SERVE NEW ADDRESS/ TRANSFERS > 28.2 TRANSFERS

Unlike a serve new address, the request will not be getting reserved, meaning no dates will be pushed and the order does not go out to Field.

Transfers occur when the facility informs you that they internally forwarded the request to another one of their locations because each office handles their own records. So we would also internally transfer the order as the new location may be under a different Area Designation. The status used will be "SERVEDTRANSFERRED REQUEST" and the Trigger will be "SENT-TRANSFER".

Example: We may have served the Fontana office, but the patient was treated at the Hawthorne office. Once the Transfer is complete, the scheduler with the Hawthorne area designation will now handle the order as their own.

Key Information

Most requests automatically come with a processing fee. The average processing fee is $15, which is dropped off at the same time our rep serves the request or will be submitted if the request is mailed. Some smaller offices may charge anywhere from $25-$50. However, always request an invoice that way we can mail the check along with a copy. This assists with pairing the correct fees to the correct order.

Any invoices over $250 need approval from our client. We do this by using the status "INVOICE/PAGECOUNT-APPROVAL NEEDED", fill out the fields accordingly, then Trigger using "SENT-ESCALATE REVIEW".

Topic: WEST REGION > 30. XRAY BREAKDOWN

Key Information

An Xray breakdown is a list of exams that were taken of the patient. The breakdown lists what exams were taken, the film counts and the cost of obtaining the images. Anytime a facility has images available we need to obtain a breakdown first, as we have to get approval from our client before paying. Breakdowns come in various formats so always keep an eye out when receiving them as you may mistake them for an invoice or billing records.

If a breakdown is received: Upload it to Import using label "_rrcorr". Your status will be "FILM -- BREAKDOWN AVAILABLE", this status does not specify that a breakdown has already received because we still need additional time for internal processing. Your Trigger will be "SENT-XRAY/FILM DESK".

text:
Document: West
Topic: WEST REGION > 31. NOTICES OF NON-COMPLIANCE > 31.3 NON-COMPLIANCE "RULE OF THUMB"

A facility is considered "non-compliant" when the due/ deposition date has passed. The facility may have stated that records have been in process for weeks without a valid explanation or if you have not had any valid contact with the facility.

On an order that was just served, the procedure is to follow up for 2-3 weeks and then send a Second Notice. If records/correspondence still have not been obtained, continue to follow up for another 2 weeks and if nothing, then send a Final Notice. After the Final Notice you want to follow up on at least one last time before sending it to Client Relations as "Non-Compliant".

NOTE: You need to be as detailed as possible and show your efforts. Request to speak to a supervisor or manager if you cannot reach the main custodian. Google other methods of contact such as an email, fax or a different phone number. Any gaps in your statuses may result in the order coming back for you to continue following up.

Topic: WEST REGION > 32. LENGTHY DELAY

Key Information

A facility is considered "Lengthy Delay" if a response will not be provided to our office within 60 days. Lengthy delay orders can stay with you for 90 days however, if a response has not been received within the 90 days, the order must be sent to Client Relations.

Client Relations will update the Client and to give them the option of continuing following up or to close the order until a response has been received.

Procedure

Lengthy delay orders can be statused every 15 days unlike normal orders where an update is needed every 5-10 days. You can use the below statuses to update:

- `DELAY-FACILITY 1ST NOTICE`
- `DELAY-FACILITY 2ND NOTICE`
- `DELAY-FACILITY 3RD NOTICE`
- `DELAY-FACILITY 4TH NOTICE`

Once the order has been open for 90 days, you can forward it to Client Relations using "NON-COMPLIANCE-HOLD FOR CLIENT RESPONSE". Your Trigger will be "SENT-ESCALATE REVIEW".

Topic: WEST REGION > 33. AUTHORIZATION REJECTIONS

Key Information

An authorization can be rejected for more multiple reasons such as missing information, invalid format, etc. When a rejection is received or the facility verbally informs you that the authorization is rejected, you must first review the authorization yourself to confirm what they are stating, is in fact true. The authorization can be found under the "Attachments".

- If their rejection is incorrect - you will push back, proceed to assist and get the order back on track.
- If their rejection is valid - you will choose the status that fits best and send the order to Client Relations by Triggering "Sent-Escalate Review". That order will sit in Client Relations for 10 days awaiting for a response from the Client.

You will receive an email in your outlook with confirmation of the fax going though or if there may have been an error.

Topic: WEST REGION > 37. DEFINITIONS

Key Information

This section provides definitions for key terms used in the document retrieval and legal process.

- ABSTRACT - Some locations will make doctors notes, emergency room records, and test results available, instead of an entire medical chart that includes nurse's notes, etc. Usually this is done at hospitals where charts can be large.
- ADDRESS SERVED - The address where a subpoena or authorization has been served via mail, fax or in person by agent.
- ADJUSTER - A designated party who reviews your claim to determine action up to and including financial compensation.
- ATTORNEY - A person who is hired or appointed to represent a party in a lawsuit. An individual who orders the request.
- AFFIDAVIT OF CUSTODIAN OF RECORDS - Affidavit signed by custodian when records, bills, films, etc. are obtained at a location.
- AFFIDAVIT OF NO RECORDS - Affidavit that states a location we have served has no records on the subject we have requested. (Also known as an ANR or CNR)
- AFFIDAVIT OF SERVICE - Affidavit that verifies an agent we have served a subpoena or authorization to a location. (California orders)
- A.K.A. - "Also Known As"
- APPLICANT - A person who applied for Worker's Compensation Benefits.
- APPLICANT COUNSEL - Counsel for Plaintiff, and/or additional counsel for the defense.
- ARBITRATOR - A person approved by the state to act as the judge during Arbitration.
- ARBITRATION - A mini trial; has all the power of a trial without a jury. A tool used by the court in an attempt to settle cases. Note: Discovery Cut Off is 15 days prior to the date of the arbitration. If the depo date is not set at least 15 days prior to the date set for arbitration, the attorney must subpoena records to the arbitration.

- AUTHORIZATION - Document signed by the patient allowing the release of his/her records by the location. (Also, could be signed by a guardian, parent, or person with a power of attorney)
- BILLING DEPARTMENT - The department/custodian of billing records for a claimant/patient.
- BUSINESS OFFICE - The department/custodian of billing records of a claimant/patient.
- CASE SETTLED - When a case settled you must discontinue work on that order. All case settled orders are be pulled and closed out within 48 hours to ensure we receive payment.
- CIVIL LAW - Law's which nation, state or city enacts to protect the privacy of all individuals. Generally, any law that is not criminal. Civil Law pertains to non-criminal matters.
- CLAIM - To demand for explanation and/or to claim loss that requires a response in writing up to financial reimbursement.
- CLAIMANT - Individual such as the patient who is the subject of the records request.
- CLAIM/CASE NUMBER - A number of ID provided by the client for tracking the request. For example, an insurance agent or adjuster may want to identify records by a specific policy or claim number.
- CLAUSE - All records being requested. Including: Medical, Billing, Films, Insurance, School, Prescription/Pharmacy, etc. Specific information can also be located in the clause, such as a treating doctor, policy number, etc.
- CLIENT - The party requesting records on the claimant/patient (Insurance Company, Law Firm).
- COMPLAINT - A document, that follows a Summons, (one page or more) which represents the case name, the case number, court, and an explanation as to why you are being sued. (Rarely do you have a summons without a complaint.)
- CONSUMER - Any person whose records are being sought. This could be medical, professional, or personal.

- COPIES - The number of copies of a record that are being requested by the client.

- EXECUTORSHIP PAPERS - Documents that indicate the person(s) authorized to obtain information on a deceased claimant.
- FACILITY - The hospital, clinic, or healthcare facility where the patient's records are located and can be obtained.
- FEES - A location can charge us a fee to obtain records, films, photos, etc.

- MEDICAL LIEN - The right of a hospital, doctor or health care provider to assert an interest in personal injury recoveries to the extent of the cost of the treatment or service provided. NOTE: Health care providers cannot delay release of records pursuant to a request because they do not have a lien signed. See Code.
- MOTION TO COMPEL - A document from the court requiring the location/facility to release records.
- MOTION TO QUASH - A legal document filed with the court demanding all work be stopped immediately on every location listed on the motion. There will be a hearing date listed on the motion at which time all parties will go before the judge and present their case as to why or why not the records should or should not be made available to copy.
- NEXT OF KIN - The person in a family to be successor after a family member has been Diseased. (The wife is deceased; her husband would be the successor.)
- NON-CONSUMER - Records of property or things that are not owned by an individual or group.
- OBJECTION - When one does not agree that records should be released either because the request is too broad or the location's records are not pertinent to the case.
- ORDER TO SHOW CAUSE - A document from the court requiring the C/R to appear before the judge and give good cause as to why they did not comply with the subpoena or other types of court requests.
- PATIENT - An individual awaiting or under medical care and treatment.
- PERSONAL APPEARANCE SUBPOENA - A subpoena that requires a person to either appear at court with or without records, or in lieu of an appearance, mail the records directly to the court.

- WORKERS' COMPENSATION APPEALS BOARD (WCAB) - The legal authority in California which handles a workers disputed claim to compensation for work related injury.

Topic: WEST REGION PROCEDURES > 2. West Region – Frequently Asked Questions > 2.1 Non-Compliance Process

Question

What is the West Region process for marking an order non-compliant?

Procedure

Complete two follow-up attempts before sending the Second Notice.
Send the Second Notice together with the request.
If the deposition date has already passed and the facility cannot be reached, send the Second Notice on the first unsuccessful attempt.
If the order is approaching or has passed the due date and the facility states that the request is still in progress, send the applicable notice.
After sending the Second Notice, complete two additional follow-up attempts.
Send the Final Notice together with the request.
After the Final Notice, complete one additional follow-up attempt.
Send the order to your Supervisor before marking it non-compliant.
After Supervisor approval, update the order to:

Non-Compliant – Hold for Client Response

Add the trigger:

Sent – Non-Compliance Review

Important Note

Document every attempt, mention all email addresses and fax number where sent notice, facility response, and escalation clearly in the order notes.

When an email bounces back:

Add a Solcom retrieval note and document all relevant details in the order.
The same information must also be updated in the Viewable Status section once the next agent will work so that the client can clearly see that the email address is invalid or incorrect.
